'''Michael M. Rozier''' (born March 1, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) for two seasons and the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for seven seasons from 1985 to 1991. He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]], winning the [[Heisman Trophy]] in 1983.  Afterward, he played for the [[Pittsburgh Maulers (1984)|Pittsburgh Maulers]] and the [[Jacksonville Bulls]] of the USFL, then played for the [[Houston Oilers]] and the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the NFL. He was inducted into the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2006.

'''Michael A. Pringle''' (born October 1, 1967) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He set or tied almost every significant [[List of Canadian Football League records|league record]] for the position. He played [[college football]] for the [[Cal State Fullerton Titans football|Cal State Fullerton Titans]], earning third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. He was twice signed by [[National Football League]] (NFL) teams, though he saw very limited playing time.

Along with [[George Reed (Canadian football)|George Reed]] and [[Johnny Bright]], Pringle is one of the players most often mentioned as being the greatest running back in CFL history. In November 2006, Pringle was voted one of the CFL's [[TSN Top 50 CFL Players|Top 50 players]] (#4) of the league's modern era by Canadian sports network [[The Sports Network|TSN]].<ref name="TSN Top 50 CFL Players">{{cite web | url = https://www.tsn.ca/cfl/feature/?fid=10867 | access-date = 2007-05-14 | title = TSN Top 50 CFL Players | publisher = [[TSN.ca]] | date = 2006-11-28}}</ref> In April 2008, Pringle was inducted into the [[Canadian Football Hall of Fame]] in his first year of eligibility.

'''Michael Schad''' (born October 4, 1963) is a Canadian former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). After his football career, he became a mortgage banker with CMG Financial located in [[Mt. Laurel, New Jersey]].{{Cn|date=April 2024}}

He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the first round with the 23rd pick of the [[1986 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1986/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He attended Moira Secondary school in [[Belleville, Ontario]]. He played his [[U Sports football|university football]] at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in Canada.  He is the only player in [[U Sports]] football history to be selected in the first round of an [[NFL draft]].<ref>[http://presto-en.usports.ca/sports/fball/2015-16/releases/onyemata Manitoba’s Onyemata becomes 12th CIS player drafted into NFL]</ref> In 1986, he won the [[J. P. Metras Trophy]] which is presented annually to the top down lineman in university football in Canada.

He played a total of 62 games with the Rams and the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], before returning to Canada in 1995 to play one year with the CFL's [[Ottawa Rough Riders]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cflapedia.com/Database/OTT.html|title=OTT}}</ref>

'''Michael L. Pruitt''' (born April 3, 1954) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (American and Canadian football)|fullback]] for 11 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1976 to 1986.  He was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the first round (seventh overall pick) of the [[1976 NFL draft]] and spent nine seasons with that club. He had five seasons with over 1,000 [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushing]] yards and was selected to play in the [[Pro Bowl]] in [[1979 Pro Bowl|1979]] and [[1980 Pro Bowl|1980]]. He also played for the [[Buffalo Bills]] for four games in 1985 and for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in 1985 and 1986.  In his NFL career, Pruitt appeared in a total of 152 games, gained 7,378 rushing yards and scored 56 [[touchdowns]].

A native of [[Chicago]], Pruitt also played [[college football]] at the fullback position for the [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue Boilermakers]] from 1973 to 1975 and was selected as a second-team running back on the [[1975 All-Big Ten Conference football team]].

Reid later began a solo recording career, releasing two studio albums for [[Columbia Records]]. He charted seven singles on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' Hot Country Singles & Tracks (now [[Hot Country Songs]]) chart as a singer, including the number one hit "[[Walk on Faith]]".

Raines was an Associated Press second-team All American his senior year at Alabama and was also chosen for the All-SEC defensive team.<ref name="sports"/> Raines was also the 1973 defensive player of the year at Alabama and played alongside Too Tall Jones in the 1973 Senior Bowl. Following the Senior Bowl Raines was drafted in the 1st. Round of the 1984 WFL draft by the California Suns and in the 6th Round of the NFL draft by the San Francisco 49ers.<ref name="bleacher"/> Raines chose to play in the NFL for the San Francisco 49ers instead of in the WFL. Following the 74 season he left the NFL for the CFL and played for the Montreal Alouettes.<ref name="stats"/> Raines played in the Canadian football league for nine seasons for three teams, Montreal (1975), Ottawa (1975–1982), Winnipeg (1982). He was named CFL Eastern Conference All-Star in 1978 and 1981.<ref name="cfl.ca"/> Raines was also named 1st Team All-Pro Defensive End in 1981 as well.<ref name="stats"/>

Following the 1982 CFL Season Raines chose to leave the CFL and join the Birmingham Stallions in the USFL. Following the 1983 Season in the USFL Raines received several honors. Raines was the only unanimous All-Pro Defensive Player voted to the 1983 First-team All-Pro USFL defensive team. Following the 1983 season Raines was traded to The Jacksonville Bulls.<ref name="upi"/> During the 1984 Season Raines was severely injured during practice, diagnosis was severe head trauma, stretched Brachial Plexus.{{Citation needed|date=April 2020}} Even though injured the Jacksonville Bulls attempted to trade Raines to The Houston Gamblers of the USFL. Upon arriving in Houston Raines was given a physical and was told he had nerve damage, possibly a slipped disk and may need surgery.{{Citation needed|date=April 2020}} He was promptly returned to Jacksonville where he finished out the season on injured reserve and retired the following year.<ref>[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=FJFVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=5j8NAAAAIBAJ&dq=mike-raines%20two%20time%20all%20star&pg=6142%2C445951 No surprise, Eskimos lead all-star team] The Leader-Post, December 2, 1981</ref>
